invariants: Version 0.6.0 identifies the portable work-environment protocol and tooling release; it does not change the separately governed Rusty Morphospace platform/runtime baseline.

Historical adoption preserves immutable terminal unit and event bytes, binds exact hashes, and records every normalization needed by current closed registries without weakening current or future validation.

A planned publication enumerates every published commit and unit, preserves non-acceptance for carried blocked work, proves source-first and planning-last order, and requires clean exact remote readback without force push.
A synchronized readback-only source leg is valid only when its revisions are equal, its commit range is empty, its bound branch and upstream match, and it makes an explicit no-acceptance claim.
An unplanned source publication is preserved through a truthful closure receipt and is never reconstructed as a retrospective push plan or relabeled as an executed-push receipt.
An early planning-only publication ordering interruption records the fault and claims neither source publication nor corrected planning-last chronology.
Published prerequisite reconciliation is confined to an exact one- or two-commit linear planning suffix and the bound receipt paths; unrelated files, source rewrites, or unbounded suffixes reject.
A separately accepted correction after immutable publication is represented by bounded additive recovery with complete commit and path attribution, not by drift tolerance.
Explicit protected-branch guards resolve symbolic local sources to the attached protected branch and reject deletion, detachment, ambiguity, or a mismatched destination.
Production aliases normalize into closed portable categories without collisions, unknown targets, or rewriting accepted historical artifacts.
Quest Accessibility foreground watchdogs remain opt-in diagnostics; they do not claim HOME ownership, device-owner authority, lock task, or managed kiosk lifecycle.
Aggregate validation executes expensive owner self-tests once per gate while nested fixtures retain structural validation and damaged-case rejection.
Existing v1 and v2 project, workspace, event, promotion, and release artifacts remain readable and are not rewritten.
